answers.runnerUp: A, if 'that' is accepted for a person
answers.reasoning: The blank stands for a person (the girl) who does the action "won", so we use "who": Is she the girl who won the first prize? "Whom" is used only when the person receives the action, and "which" is used for things.

The sentence simply states a fact and ends with a full stop, so it is a declarative (statement) sentence. It is not an order, a question or an exclamation.

The correct spelling is A-P-P-O-I-N-T-M-E-N-T: double p, single t, and "-ment" at the end.
A cobbler is a person who mends shoes and sandals, that is, footwear. A person who mends clothes is a tailor.
"Earlier" means at a time before; its opposite is "later", at a time after. "Former" and "previous" mean almost the same as earlier, and "latter" means the second of two things.
"Momentous" means very important or of great significance. "Insignificant" is its opposite.
With "the" and a whole trip being compared, we need the superlative of "bad", which is "worst". "Most worse", "more worse" and "worser" are all incorrect forms.
"Gigantic" means huge, like a giant, so it means very big.
A literate person can read and write. The opposite is made with the prefix "il-": illiterate. The other words do not exist.
The plural of "mouse" is "mice", not "mouses", so this pair is incorrect. Knife-knives, woman-women and deer-deer are all correct.
The saying is "Birds of a feather flock together": people who are alike like to stay together.
"Later" tells us when the doctor will see you, so it describes the verb "see". A word that tells when, where or how is an adverb.
This is one quick action in the past, so the simple past tense fits: Seeing the wounded bird, she called her mother. "Call" and "calling" do not fit after "she" here.

"Unless" means "if not": Manjeet cannot drive unless he has a licence, that is, he cannot drive if he does not have a licence. "Although" would mean he cannot drive even with a licence, which does not make sense here.

answers.value: Water vapour cools and condenses around a particle of dust or salt
answers.reasoning: In cloud seeding, tiny particles such as salt or silver iodide are sprayed into clouds. Water vapour cools and condenses around these particles into drops, which grow heavy and fall as rain.
